title: Buckaroo Bowl I: Habibsters Win the First Crown, Ben Dover Wins the Ladder Nobody Wanted
dek: Kaushal turned the league's inaugural season into a wire-to-wire statement, while Mekhi scored the most points and still went 6-8, and Sonny's commissionership opened with a last-place finish on his own website.
body: Every dynasty needs a first chapter, and the Buckaroo Football League's opened in 2023 with six teams, one draft, and zero idea of what was coming. When the dust settled, Kaushal's Habibsters owned the regular season, the playoffs, and the very first Buckaroo Bowl trophy. Nobody else's name is engraved on Bowl I, and nobody else's ever will be. That's how history works, and it's going to be brought up at every draft for the rest of time.

Habibsters went 10-4, took the No. 1 seed, and piled up 1528.8 points, second-most in the league. Right behind them was Alan's Team Pillbert at 9-5 and 1499.3 points, and Philly authored the single loudest afternoon of the year with a 156.18 explosion in Week 3. Randy's The fumblers grabbed the No. 3 seed at an extremely balanced 7-7, a record that says "playoff team" and "coin flip" at the same time. The final playoff spot went to Mekhi's Dawgs at 6-8.

And here's the stat that should be framed and hung in the league office: Dawgs led all six teams with 1542.8 points. Mekhi scored more than the champion, more than everyone, and still finished two games under .500. Kai's lineup did its job week after week, and the schedule apparently kept sending him opponents who picked that exact week to have the game of their lives. If fantasy football had a Cy Young for run support, he'd be the poster child for not getting any.

The playoffs ran on two-week totals, and the top seeds held serve. Habibsters handled Dawgs 237.54 to 196.12, ending the points champ's run and confirming that Mekhi's scoring crown came with no hardware. Team Pillbert outlasted The fumblers 234.86 to 216.44 in the tighter semifinal, sending Alan to the big game and setting up the villain-versus-favorite final the league didn't know it needed. Randy recovered to finish third, with Mekhi fourth.

Buckaroo Bowl I wasn't close. Habibsters dropped 251.36 over two weeks to Team Pillbert's 192.08, a 59-point margin that turned the championship into a coronation. Alan had the best single week of the season and the second-best record, and still got run off the field when it mattered most. Kaushal, meanwhile, set the speed limit for everyone who would follow, and blew right past it.

At the other end, the consolation ladder delivered a twist. Ramon's Araleasers went 4-10, posted the league's fewest points at 1375.3, and owned the season's low point with a 65.9 in Week 9, but Brucie climbed out of the cellar when it counted. That left Sonny's Ben Dover, a 6-8 team that scored 1413.3 points, holding the league's first last-place finish. The commissioner built the website, and his own team became its first cautionary tale.

One final number tells you everything about the league's opening act: zero trades. Six managers spent an entire season staring at each other's rosters and nobody blinked, which surprised no one who has ever tried to pry a player out of Randy's hands. Kaushal didn't need a deal anyway. He had the best record, the top seed, and the first ring, and the other five had an entire offseason to figure out how to stop it from happening again.
